title: Film Thickness Measurement - Film Non-Uniformity Detection on Archer 750
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Archer 750 system to detect and classify Film Non-Uniformity defects during final inspection inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Film Non-Uniformity defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Archer 750 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Archer 750
- Inspection Type: Film Thickness Measurement
- Target Defect: Film Non-Uniformity
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all Archer 750 systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for final inspection monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Archer 750
Software Version: v15.1.170
Recipe: FILM_THICKNESS_MEASUREMENT_28nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (143 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Archer 750 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Film Thickness Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Film Non-Uniformity defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 92 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.9% for Film Thickness Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-02-21
Wafers Tested: 35
Total Defects Found: 4157
Defect Density: 1323.22 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 4.2%
Capture Rate: 94.6%
Test Duration: 165 minutes
System Uptime: 96.7%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Archer 750 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Film Non-Uniformity at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
